info.bio:
Tom Jones, nombre artístico de Sir Thomas John Woodward, es un cantante, actor y Caballero de la Corona Británica nacido en Treforest, Pontypridd, una localidad cerca de Cardiff, Gales el 7 de junio de 1940 y ha vendido cerca de 70 millones de discos en todo el mundo.

Jones se hizo conocido en la década de 1960 por su extravagante estilo y por su sensualidad, elementos que han sido claves en su imagen como artista.

Su carrera se inicia en 1963 cuando era vocalista del grupo Tommy Scott & The Senators

scenes.name: El pop de papá y mamá
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Los adultos compraban LPs (a 32 chelines frente a los 6 de un single) y también muchos singles, de modo que la lista británica de 1965 era esquizofrénica: los Stones y los Beatles competían con lo que los adolescentes llamaban «música de papás y mamás», Ken Dodd, los Seekers, los Bachelors o Jim Reeves. La banda sonora de The Sound of Music encabezó la lista de LPs casi todo 1965 y 1966. Los adolescentes más jóvenes encontraban nuevos ídolos como los Walker Brothers, baladistas melodramáticos a lo Spector.

podcast.title: Early Best New Artist Winner
podcast.body: Tom Jones was an early recipient of the Best New Artist prize, which was launched in the early 1960s as a way for the Academy to acknowledge young performers whose music aligned with voters' preferences. "Early winners of the prize included Bobby Darren, Robert Goulet and Tom Jones."

xref.title: Inspiration for "You Know My Name" (2006)
xref.body: While writing "You Know My Name" for "Casino Royale," Chris Cornell listened repeatedly to Tom Jones's "Thunderball" (1965) and Paul McCartney's "Live and Let Die" (1973) for inspiration. He aimed to create something new that still resonated with Bond tradition, leading to a critically acclaimed and Grammy-nominated song. "And one song that he listened to over and over again was Tom Jones's Thunderball a theme from 1965. He also listened to Live in Let Die a lot."

xref.title: Early Drumming and Diverse Collaborations
xref.body: Chrissy Lee began drumming at age four in a Salvation Army band. Throughout her career, she performed with a wide array of renowned artists including Frank Sinatra, Fats Domino, Tom Jones, and Dinah Washington. She also became heavily involved in education, conducting drum clinics globally. "She started drumming in a Salvation Army band when she was just four years old."
